subject: Clarify hosted metering: streaming frames, billable-token rounding, and commit tiers
messages:
From: Elena Morales <elena.morales@novayard.com>
To: dev_patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jake Simmons <jake.simmons@novayard.com>, Novayard Billing <billing@novayard.com>
Date: Thu, 20 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Question on hosted metering details for SOW v2

Hi Dev,

Thanks for the updated SOW. Before we circulate to procurement I need to confirm a couple of metering mechanics so our finance team can map predicted spend to quarters:

1) Streaming / chunked responses: if a single user request streams N incremental deltas (e.g., partial tokens every 200ms), how are those billed? Are the streamed bytes counted as they are emitted or collapsed into one final request count?

2) Rounding: we saw references to "per-token" charges and an example note about "round up to nearest 1 token" in your pricing appendix. Do you round per request, per second, per minute, or on aggregated monthly usage?

3) Commit tiers and overage math: we want to understand how bursting above committed monthly tokens impacts effective unit price (e.g., if we are in the 1M-5M commit band and exceed it by 10% in a month). Is overage charged at the nominal list rate, or is there an averaging/proration step?

Can you provide the exact contract language (one paragraph per item) you expect in the SOW for these mechanics? Our legal will drop in redlines if needed.

Appreciate the quick reply — our quarterly forecasting meeting is next Wednesday.

Best,
Elena
Director, Product 
NovaYard

Subject: Re: Question on hosted metering details for SOW v2

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear list. Shared below are concise, contract-ready snippets we usually propose; I included a short worked example for streaming to make the math concrete. Happy to iterate.

1) Streaming responses (metering): 
"Streaming responses are measured at token emission time. Each token emitted by the model (partial or final) counts toward the customer's billable token total. For streaming protocols that emit partial tokens or deltas, Redwood collapses whitespace-normalized tokens into model tokens before counting; intermediate partial bytes are not separately billed. Example: a single streaming generation that emits 100 incremental tokens over 10 deltas will be billed as 100 billable tokens."

2) Rounding and aggregation: 
"Billable tokens are aggregated by calendar month per account. For billing purposes Redwood rounds billed token totals to the nearest whole token at the account-month granularity (no per-request rounding). Example: if aggregated usage is 1,234,567.4 tokens for August, the billed amount will be 1,234,567 tokens."

3) Commit tiers, overage, and proration: 
"Customers may select a monthly committed token quantity and associated tiered unit price. If actual usage in a billing month exceeds the committed quantity, overages are billed at the published overage rate for the next tier; no retroactive averaging is applied. If a customer reduces a committed quantity mid-term, the new commitment is prorated for the remainder of the billing period. True-ups at quarter-end may be applied if included in the SOW."

Worked streaming example (for clarity):
- Request A streams content in 5 deltas; total tokenized output = 120 tokens
- Request B returns immediate non-streaming output = 80 tokens
- Account monthly aggregated tokens = 200 tokens (120 + 80) => billed = 200 tokens

Let's sync with legal on any precise phrasing — copying Laura and Karthik for pricing/contract alignment.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Elena — quick legal/pricing clarifications and one suggested tweak to the rounding language: 

We generally avoid "nearest" rounding in contract text because it can create ambiguity. Proposed adjustment: round down fractional tokens at account-month granularity (we have historically done that to avoid billing disputes for <1 token fractions that arise from internal aggregation). Alternatively, we can explicitly say "round to the nearest whole token, with .5 rounded up" if you prefer symmetric rounding. Which does NovaYard prefer?

Also on overage math: we charge overages at the published overage rate for the next tier for the remainder of the billing month. We do not retroactively change the unit price applied to the committed volume in that month. If you want an averaging/step-down structure, that's a special pricing accommodation (we can propose a blended overage rate as a contract appendix).

Sample revised rounding paragraph: 
"Billable tokens are aggregated by calendar month per account. For billing purposes Redwood truncates fractional token totals to the whole-token integer at the account-month granularity (fractions are not billed). Example: if aggregated usage is 1,234,567.9 tokens for August, the billed amount will be 1,234,567 tokens."

Karthik — dropping to you for the proposed overage rate table and whether we want to offer NovaYard a blended overage for the first three months if they commit to a 12-month term.

Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Contracts and Commercial
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Question on hosted metering details for SOW v2

Thanks — quick pricing addition and an operational note: 

Proposed overage structure (example for illustration; final numbers in SOW exhibit):
- Commit band A: 0 - 1,000,000 tokens/month => base price $0.00030/token; overage (if > commit) charged at $0.00035/token
- Commit band B: 1,000,001 - 5,000,000 tokens/month => base price $0.00025/token; overage charged at $0.00030/token
- Commit band C: 5,000,001+ tokens/month => base price $0.00020/token; overage charged at $0.00022/token

Operational note on streaming: our hosted runtime increments KV cache and token accounting as soon as tokens are committed to the response buffer (i.e., emission time), which means billing visibility in usage dashboards will be near-real-time. However, we only finalize the account-month aggregate for invoicing at month close after lightweight post-processing (dedup and normalization) — that post-process is where fractional token truncation will be applied.

For NovaYard I can tentatively offer a blended overage rate equal to (base price * 0.9) for the first two months post-go-live if they sign a 12-month contract and commit to Band B. I'll put that in the commercial term sheet.

-Karthik
Head of Commercial Pricing
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Question on hosted metering details for SOW v2

Thanks all — that is super helpful and clear. Two quick items before procurement + legal run this through: 

1) Rounding preference: NovaYard prefers symmetric rounding (".5 rounds up") rather than truncation. If Redwood is uncomfortable with that operationally, we can accept truncation but will ask for a 25bps credit on the first invoice to offset the asymmetry.

2) Blended overage pilot: we accept the Band B commitment (1M-5M) for 12 months if Redwood will include the blended overage (base*0.9) for months 1-2 post-go-live and the blended rate explicitly in the SOW exhibit.

If you can send a single-paragraph SOW appendix with the agreed language for: streaming metering, rounding (symmetric), and the Band B blended pilot we will push to procurement on Wednesday. Also include the DocuSign link for signatures.

Appreciate the responsiveness — cc'ing our billing lead to speed PO prep.

Best,
Elena
Director, Product
NovaYard
